clue.text: Bean variety gets carted initially in van that's horse-drawn

definitions.note: a relative clause standing for a thing that horses pull, i.e. a horse-drawn vehicle

indicators.note: the van is the front of a column, so the letter is shifted to the very front of the word

parts.note: the haricot is a variety of bean

indicators.note: initially picks out the opening letter of carted

parts.note: first letter of carted

explanation.surface: A kind of bean is being carted about in a horse-drawn van, as if on its way to market.
explanation.walkthrough: HARICOT already contains a C; 'carted initially' names that C, and 'in van' moves it from the middle of the word to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: A chariot is a two-wheeled vehicle pulled by horses, used in ancient warfare and racing.

clue.text: Raucous-sounding raven, possibly, essential listening

indicators.note: what we hear when listening is a sound-alike of the words before it

parts.note: a raven is one kind of crow (possibly signals an example), and essential means key: CROW plus KEY

explanation.surface: The harsh call of a raven is presented as something you simply must hear.
explanation.walkthrough: Say CROW KEY aloud and you hear the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A croaky voice is hoarse and harsh, which is what raucous-sounding describes.

clue.text: Changed or added missing pages — a thousand inserted

indicators.note: inserted tells us the thousand is put inside the other letters
missing means the pages are left out of the word for added

parts.note: appended means added on
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand

explanation.surface: Someone describes an edited document: altered, pages taken out, and a large number slipped in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'added' is not the definition here but a synonym to be shortened; PP is the standard abbreviation for pages.
explanation.definitionFit: Amended means altered or revised, as a law or text is changed by amendment.

clue.text: Increase in US money swamps rock group

indicators.note: to swamp is to engulf, so the money surrounds the band

parts.note: a cent is a unit of US money
R.E.M. is an American rock band

explanation.surface: An increase in American money overwhelms a rock band, like a payday dwarfing the musicians.
explanation.definitionFit: An increment is a step up or addition, such as a rise in salary.

clue.text: Move briskly after wrong turns

indicators.note: turns means the word for wrong is read backwards

parts.note: a tort is a civil wrong in law

explanation.surface: After taking a wrong turn, someone hurries along to make up time.
explanation.walkthrough: TORT is the legal term for a civil wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: To trot is to go at a pace faster than walking, as a horse or a hurrying person does.

clue.text: Minor disturbance often seen at the seaside?

definitions.text: Minor disturbance often seen at the seaside?

parts.words: Minor disturbance often seen at the seaside
parts.note: a small ripple in the water at the shore, not a little scuffle on the promenade

explanation.walkthrough: 'Minor disturbance' suggests a small fracas, but the disturbance is on the surface of the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: A wavelet is a small wave or ripple, a slight disturbance of water seen lapping on beaches.

clue.text: Using other hand, Walt strips off something round his forearm?

indicators.note: off suggests the letters are disordered, in an anagram sense of not right
the other hand to left is right, so L (left) is swapped for R (right)

parts.note: taken as written as the anagram fodder, with its L changed

explanation.surface: Walt, switching hands, takes off something fastened round his arm.
explanation.walkthrough: Swap the L of WALT STRIPS for an R, then rearrange the letters as 'off' signals.
explanation.definitionFit: A wrist strap is a band worn round the lower forearm, as on a watch or a sports support.

clue.text: Consumer taking only produce like 10 11 22, say, in van

definitions.text: Consumer taking only produce like 10 11 22, say

indicators.note: in places the abbreviation for say inside the word van

parts.note: EG (for example) is the abbreviation meaning say

explanation.surface: Someone eating red kidney beans in a van is described as a plant-only diner.
explanation.walkthrough: Clues 10, 11 and 22 give RED KIDNEY BEANS, a plant food; 'say' does double duty in the surface but is the EG here.
explanation.definitionFit: A vegan eats only plant foods, avoiding meat, dairy and eggs, so pulses are typical fare.

clue.text: Old West town in a Mailer novel

indicators.note: novel as an adjective means new, so the letters come in a new order

parts.note: taken as written, the fodder; Norman Mailer was a US novelist

explanation.surface: A frontier town features in a book by Norman Mailer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' looks like a book by Mailer but is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Laramie in Wyoming was a famous frontier settlement of the Wild West, subject of TV westerns.

clue.text: Eats inside — it's an orderly quality

indicators.note: inside says the word for eats is placed within the other

parts.note: 'tis is an old contraction of it is
dines means eats

explanation.surface: Eating indoors is praised as a sign of a neat, well-kept home.
explanation.definitionFit: Tidiness is the state of being neat and well arranged, a quality of order.

clue.text: Fiddling about comes before burning, maybe

indicators.note: comes before says the word for about stands ahead of the word for fiddling

parts.note: over can mean about, as in fussing over something
cooking, as in cooking the books, means fiddling or falsifying

explanation.surface: Messing about in the kitchen is followed by something getting burnt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fiddling' looks musical or fidgety; in the sense of cooking the books it is COOKING.
explanation.definitionFit: Burning food is an example of cooking it too long, hence 'maybe'.

clue.text: Knock back the German wine

indicators.note: knocking back sends the German article the other way, reading it in reverse

parts.note: der is a German word for the

explanation.surface: Someone downs a glass of German wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Knock back' suggests drinking quickly, but it signals reversal.
explanation.definitionFit: Red is the short name for red wine, ordered as 'a glass of red'.

clue.text: Child finally can have toy organ

parts.note: a kid is a child

indicators.note: finally picks the final letter of each of the three following words

parts.note: last letter of can
last letter of have
last letter of toy

explanation.surface: A child at last gets a toy organ to play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'organ' looks musical alongside 'toy', but it is the body part.
explanation.definitionFit: The kidney is a bodily organ that filters blood, so it fits organ in the anatomical sense.

clue.text: Stand-in crew at first crazy about trip's start

indicators.note: at first says the stretch after it comes first, ahead of the word for crew
about here means turned round, so the word for crazy is read backwards

parts.note: nuts means crazy

indicators.note: start picks the first letter of trip's

parts.note: first letter of trip's
to man a ship is to crew it

explanation.surface: A film crew's stand-in goes crazy at the start of a trip.
explanation.walkthrough: The sense is 'crew, at first crazy about trip's start': STUN plus T leads, then MAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A stuntman stands in for an actor to perform dangerous scenes, a body double.

clue.text: French sister claims some land adjoining Catholic church

indicators.note: claims means holds onto, so the sister wraps round the land and Catholic

parts.note: soeur is French for sister

indicators.note: adjoining says the abbreviation sits right beside the land

parts.note: an acre is a measure of land

explanation.surface: A French nun lays claim to a plot of land next to a Catholic church.
explanation.walkthrough: SOEUR is the French for sister, a nun or a sibling.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sacré-Coeur is the white-domed basilica on Montmartre in Paris.

clue.text: Almost decides to melt down metal toys

indicators.note: melting down reshapes the metal, as the letters are reshaped into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, the anagram fodder

explanation.surface: Someone nearly makes up their mind to melt down some metal toys.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Almost' looks like a shortening instruction, but it is part of the fodder: ALMOST plus DECIDES.
explanation.definitionFit: Die-cast models are small replica vehicles made by forcing molten metal into moulds, collected as toys.

clue.text: Reorganise university course to allocate work elsewhere

indicators.note: reorganise says the letters are put in a different order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A university restructures a course so its teaching is contracted out.
explanation.definitionFit: To outsource is to contract jobs out to an external supplier instead of doing them in-house.

clue.text: Ex-boozers to drink 1.2 pints? Great — it's 6 cooking water!

indicators.note: to drink is to take in, so the ex-boozers take the other letters inside

parts.note: AA is Alcoholics Anonymous, a group of former drinkers
a quart is two pints, so 1.2 pints is three-fifths of a quart: the first three of the five letters of QUART
fab, short for fabulous, means great

explanation.surface: Reformed drinkers are offered a pint-ish measure and cheerfully told it is just cooking water.
explanation.walkthrough: 6 refers to clue 6, VEGAN. Three-fifths of QUART is QUA, as 1.2 pints is three-fifths of a quart.
explanation.definitionFit: Aquafaba is the liquid from cooked chickpeas, used by vegans as an egg-white substitute.

clue.text: Supplies officer with fourth kind of tape

parts.note: a quarter is a fourth part
a master tape is the original recording from which copies are made

explanation.surface: An army stores officer is equipped with a quarter and some special tape.
explanation.definitionFit: A quartermaster is the military officer in charge of provisions, quarters and equipment.

clue.text: Material that's elastic — Lycra, I see

indicators.note: elastic means stretchy and flexible, so the letters are bent into a new shape

parts.note: taken as written
the letter C sounds like see

explanation.surface: Someone recognises a stretchy fabric as Lycra.
explanation.walkthrough: 'elastic' looks like a description of the material but signals the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Acrylic is a synthetic fibre and fabric, a man-made textile.

clue.text: Argument against joining encounter

indicators.note: joining says the two words are attached one after the other

parts.note: a run-in is a quarrel or argument
to can mean against, as in face to face or set to the wall

explanation.surface: A case is made against bringing two things together.
explanation.definitionFit: To run into someone is to meet them by chance.

clue.text: Get knight covering king, giving check

definitions.note: second meaning: to examine or test

indicators.note: covering means wrapping round, so the get-plus-knight letters enclose the king

parts.note: to see is to get, in the sense of understand
CR, Carolus Rex, is the abbreviation for King Charles
N is the chess notation for a knight

explanation.surface: A chess player blocks check by moving a knight in front of the king.
explanation.walkthrough: The chess surface is a disguise: 'Get' is SEE, as in 'I get it', and CR (Latin Carolus Rex) is a king; 'giving' links wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To screen people is to check or vet them, as in screening for a disease.

clue.text: Exercises requiring introductions of an extensive range of pens

indicators.note: the introductions of words are their first letters, taken from the next four words

parts.note: first letter of an
first letter of extensive
first letter of range
first letter of of
Bics are ballpoint pens, from the Bic brand

explanation.surface: A workout routine apparently calls for a wide selection of pens.
explanation.definitionFit: Aerobics is a form of rhythmic exercise to raise heart rate, done in classes.

clue.text: Energy-packing bars and maybe canned food

indicators.note: packing means holding inside, so the word for bars holds the energy symbol

parts.note: to bar is to ban
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Energy bars and tinned food sound like a hiker's provisions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Energy-packing bars' reads as snack bars, but bars are BANS.
explanation.definitionFit: Beans are often bought in tins, as with baked beans, so canned food is an example.

clue.text: Charlie may pop back for a drink

parts.note: Charlie is C in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: back means the following words are read in reverse

parts.note: can, meaning be allowed to, is a synonym of may
to pop, as in pop out, is to go

explanation.surface: Charlie may drop in again for a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Cognac is a brandy from western France, served as an after-dinner spirit.

clue.text: Long throw striking opener

indicators.note: striking out the opener deletes the first letter of the word for throw

parts.note: to pitch is to throw

explanation.surface: A long throw hits the batsman opening the innings.
explanation.walkthrough: An opener is the batsman who starts the innings in cricket.
explanation.definitionFit: To itch for something is to long for it, to want it restlessly.

clue.text: All I ask in return is containing trouble

indicators.note: in return means the hidden letters are read backwards
the words are said to contain the answer, which sits within them

explanation.surface: A modest plea: all I want back is to keep a problem under control.
explanation.definitionFit: To ail is to trouble or afflict, as in 'what ails you?'

clue.text: A banned substance coating man and ape, this defoliant

indicators.note: coating means covering round, so the A and E surround the man and ape

parts.note: E is short for ecstasy, an illegal drug
a gent is a man
orang is short for orang-utan, an ape

explanation.surface: A prohibited chemical covers a man and an ape, presented as a weedkiller.
explanation.definitionFit: Agent Orange was the herbicide sprayed by the US in Vietnam to strip foliage.

clue.text: One denouncing a druggie injecting small amount

indicators.note: injecting puts the small amount into the other letters, as a needle does

parts.note: a user is a drug-taker
cc, a cubic centimetre, is a small amount of liquid

explanation.surface: A drug addict is reported while injecting a small dose.
explanation.definitionFit: An accuser is someone who charges or blames another, denouncing them.

clue.text: Dance with any number following garden party

indicators.note: following says the pair after it comes later, after garden and party

parts.note: to hoe is to garden
a do is a party
N stands for any number in maths

explanation.surface: A dance takes place after a garden party.
explanation.definitionFit: A hoedown is a lively American folk dance or the social gathering where it happens.
